candidates.theme_relation: Consumer ecommerce and travel merchants can improve gross conversion and economics if false declines, chargebacks and policy abuse are reduced.

candidates.why_underfollowed: Small-cap post-IPO fintech/software name whose value may be screened as generic fraud software while the chokepoint is merchant authorization quality, chargeback economics and ecommerce conversion. evidence.claim: Riskified describes itself as a leader in ecommerce fraud and risk intelligence and reported 2025 merchant products including fraud/risk intelligence, chargeback management and representment services.
Riskified's 2024 filing reported merchants integrated on its AI-powered ecommerce risk intelligence platform generated $141.2B of GMV in 2024, up from $123.1B in 2023.
Riskified market-cap sources reported approximately $684M-$690M around late May/June 2026, placing it in the $300M-$1B hunting bucket.
ACI Worldwide's 2024 10-K says its customers operate across verticals including general retail, grocery, hospitality, dining, travel and ticketing, fuel and telecommunications.

ACI's 2024 10-K describes payment orchestration capabilities and ACI Fraud Management for merchants and billers using AI technology, behavioral analytics, customizable fraud strategies and consortium data.
A June 2026 market-cap source reported ACI Worldwide market capitalization around $4.44B.

Bread Financial's annual report describes primary products including private-label and co-brand credit card programs with retailers and brand partners, direct-to-consumer cards, Bread Pay products and Bread Savings products.
A market-cap source reported Bread Financial market capitalization around $3.6B in May/June 2026.

Cardlytics' filing says its platform supports marketers across retail, restaurant, travel and entertainment, direct-to-consumer, grocery and gas, and uses FI and merchant data partners for loyalty and engagement campaigns.

Public market-cap sources for Cardlytics in June 2026 vary materially, with some reporting tens of millions and another around $274M, supporting a micro-cap/speculative-exception label rather than a clean $300M-plus candidate.

A Mastercard-sponsored Datos Insights study cited by TechRadar estimated sellers would lose $15B to fraudulent chargebacks in 2025, with chargeback volume projected to rise from 261M in 2025 to 324M by 2028.
evidence.source_title: Businesses globally are set to lose $15 billion in 2025 because of fraudulent chargebacks, says Mastercard

memory_update.text: RSKD should be retained as a pure-play underfollowed candidate for ecommerce fraud, chargeback protection and merchant risk intelligence; promote only if GMV, merchant retention and chargeback expense trends confirm scalable unit economics.

ACIW maps to the payment orchestration and fraud-management chokepoint for retail/travel/restaurant merchants; its underappreciation risk is that the market may treat it as legacy payments software rather than checkout reliability infrastructure.

BFH is a higher-risk alternative-credit infrastructure candidate tied to retailer private-label/co-brand credit and loyalty; later layers must separate merchant-infrastructure value from consumer credit-cycle risk.

CDLX is a speculative micro-cap exception for loyalty and bank-linked commerce data; require survival checks on liquidity, Nasdaq compliance, FI partner durability and revenue stabilization before further promotion.

Need a follow-up search for US-listed payment gateways/orchestration names beyond ACIW and large-cap references, including whether any private chargeback specialists have public parents or meaningful disclosed subsidiaries.

node: Consumer payments, fraud prevention, chargeback management, loyalty, and alternative credit infrastructure
summary: Expanded the universe around merchant payments risk infrastructure rather than consumer-facing lenders or mega-cap card networks. The strongest underfollowed fits are Riskified for ecommerce fraud/chargeback intelligence, ACI Worldwide for merchant payment orchestration plus fraud tooling, Bread Financial for retailer private-label/co-brand credit and loyalty financing infrastructure, and Cardlytics as a speculative micro-cap commerce-media/loyalty-data exception. Mastercard, Visa, PayPal, Adyen, Shopify and Block are useful reference anchors but were intentionally excluded from the candidate list because this pass emphasizes less obvious small/mid-cap and second-order infrastructure exposure.
